raw_response:
*Sitting on the edge of my courtyard, thinking through the year ahead...*

Forty years on this land. My father farmed it before me. Eleven point four mu isn't a big farm, but it's mine. Six mouths in the household, though my eldest son works construction in Handan most months and the daughter-in-law has a job in town. So really it's me and my wife doing most of the work, with the grandkids helping when school's out.

Let me think about how I'm splitting the land this year, same as last year really. About 5.4 mu in the wheat-maize rotation — that's my reliable food and cash. The other 6 mu I keep in cotton. I know cotton prices aren't what they were ten years ago, and a lot of the young farmers around here have given up on it. But I've been growing cotton since I was a young man, I know how to do it, and the subsidy helps. My wife does most of the picking with her sister.

**On the wheat (already in the ground since last October):**

The wheat is greening up now. This week or next I need to do my spring topdressing — I'll spread urea, about 12 kg per mu, right before the irrigation. The extension station fellow keeps saying 10 is enough but I've always done a bit more and my yields are decent, around 450 kg per mu in a normal year. I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at planting last fall, about 30 kg per mu, so the phosphorus and potassium are already in the soil.

Irrigation — I'll water at greening, then jointing, then again at grain filling. Three times if the spring rain comes, four if it stays dry like last year. The well is shared with two other households so we have to coordinate. Electricity for pumping costs me about 30-40 yuan per mu per watering.

I'll spray herbicide once for the broadleaf weeds, and watch for aphids in May — if I see them bad I'll spray, otherwise leave it alone. No need to waste money.

**On the maize (planted right after wheat harvest in June):**

The window between wheat harvest and maize planting is tight, less than a week. I hire the combine for the wheat (60 yuan per mu) and the same fellow has a no-till planter that drops the maize seed right into the stubble. I buy hybrid seed every year from the agricultural supply shop in town — Zhengdan 958 usually, or whatever the shop owner recommends. About 50 yuan per mu for seed.

I put all the fertilizer down at planting with the seed — a compound fertilizer at about 40 kg per mu. If the maize looks pale at the big trumpet stage in August I'll topdress urea, maybe 10 kg per mu. Usually I do.

Maize doesn't need much water if the summer rains come, but if July is dry I'll irrigate once or twice. Spray herbicide right after planting before the weeds come up. Expect about 500 kg per mu — my best year was 580, my worst was 380 in that drought summer a few years back.

**On the cotton (planting in late April):**

Cotton is the most work and the most worry. I prepare the land in early April — I plow it myself with the small tractor I share with my brother, then make ridges. I lay plastic mulch and plant Bt cotton seed in mid-to-late April, around April 20-25 depending on the soil temperature. The Bt seed is more expensive but I don't have to spray as much for bollworm.

Fertilizer for cotton — I put down compound fertilizer before laying the mulch, then topdress urea around flowering in July, total maybe 14 kg of nitrogen per mu. Some neighbors put down more but cotton doesn't always pay back the extra.

The hardest part is the picking — three or four rounds from September into October. My wife and her sister do most of it, and we hire two or three village women for a few days during the heaviest pick. Hired labor for picking runs about 1 yuan per jin these days.

I'll spray for aphids and bollworm a few times even with Bt — there are still other pests. And weeding between the rows once or twice in summer.

Yield around 250 jin per mu of seed cotton in a good year. Price has been weak, around 8-9 yuan per jin for seed cotton lately. The subsidy makes the difference between profit and break-even.

**Total cash I need to put up:** I figure around 5,500-6,000 yuan for inputs across all three crops this year. That's tight but manageable. We have some savings from last year, and the wheat sale in June will help cover the maize inputs.
